comm.t: The hymn of the gods (11.2–35) is over, and the Goddess answers it. This is her first speech since the death of Śumbha; within the frame it is still Medhas who reports it to Suratha and Samādhi (the ṛṣi of 11.1).

sandhi.note: ā + a → ā. The final m of अहम् becomes anusvāra before the s of सुरगणाः (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).
-āḥ before the voiced v: the visarga (as ru) becomes y, and before a consonant that y is always lost, leaving -ā.
Final t (voiced to d at word end, 8.2.39) becomes the nasal n before the m of मनसा; then ā + i → e (मनसा + इच्छथ → मनसेच्छथ).

samasa.sense: the bestower of boons — the title with which she offers the gods their wish

morph.note: Imperative, 2nd plural, ātmanepada, of √वृ (svādi, stem वृणु-): ‘choose for yourselves’. The middle voice suits a choice made for one’s own benefit.
√दा forms its present on the substitute stem यच्छ-; with प्र, ‘to give, to grant’. The present stands for the immediate future: ‘I (will) grant it’.
Present of √इष् (tudādi), stem इच्छ-, 2nd plural: ‘you wish’.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) सुरगणाः, अहं वरदा (अस्मि)। यत् वरं मनसा इच्छथ, जगताम् उपकारकं तं वृणुध्वम्; (तं) प्रयच्छामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: A nominal sentence (अहं वरदा) and the address; then a relative clause (यत् वरं … इच्छथ) picked up by तम्, the object of the imperative वृणुध्वम्; प्रयच्छामि closes with an implied object.
mantras.lit: I am the giver of boons, O hosts of gods. The boon which you desire in your mind — choose that, beneficial to the worlds; I grant it.
mantras.tr: I am the giver of boons, you hosts of gods. Choose the boon your minds desire, one that will benefit the worlds, and I shall grant it.
mantras.tr_note: The object of प्रयच्छामि is supplied (‘it’), and the present is rendered as a promise (‘I shall grant’).

comm.t: Pleased by the hymn, the Goddess offers a boon, as she did after the hymn of chapter 4 (4.32). She sets one condition herself: the boon is to be जगताम् उपकारकम्, of benefit to the worlds, not to the gods alone.

Each of the text’s great hymns is followed by a boon (1.95–98 to Viṣṇu from the asuras, 4.32–37 and here). In the Śākta reading the pattern teaches that praise is answered: the Goddess is वरदा, the one who grants what is asked.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) gives the same epithet as a name: 331, वरदा. Here it is the Goddess’s own word for herself in the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; the shared title is a shared Śākta idea, not a borrowing between the texts.

flags.uncertain: यत् … तम्: the relative is neuter and the correlative masculine. Read here as a generic ‘whatever (boon)’; it may also be a loose agreement for यम्. The sense is the same either way.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (its first member सर्वाबाधा is a karmadhāraya: सर्वाः च ताः आबाधाः च)
samasa.sense: the removal of every trouble that besets the three worlds

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (अस्मद्वैरि)
samasa.literal: the destruction of the enemies of us
samasa.sense: the slaying of our enemies — as she has just slain Śumbha and Niśumbha

morph.note: Gerundive of √कृ with ṇyat (कृ + य, vṛddhi → कार्य): ‘to be done’. The agent goes in the instrumental (त्वया), the thing to be done is the grammatical subject; neuter singular agrees with प्रशमनम् and विनाशनम् taken together as one task.
Taddhita with vṛddhi of the first syllable: त्रि-लोक → त्रैलोक्य ‘the three worlds as a whole’ (neuter collective).

mantras.anvaya: (हे) अखिलेश्वरि, त्रैलोक्यस्य सर्वाबाधाप्रशमनम् (तथा) अस्मद्वैरिविनाशनम् एवम् एव त्वया कार्यम्।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive construction with the gerundive: the two nouns of action are the subjects, कार्यम् the predicate, त्वया the agent; एवम् एव points back to what she has just done.
mantras.lit: O Queen of all, the quelling of all afflictions of the three worlds — and in just this way the destruction of our enemies — is to be done by you.
mantras.tr: O Sovereign of all, quell every affliction of the three worlds, and destroy our enemies just as you have done now.
mantras.tr_note: The gerundive (‘is to be done by you’) is rendered as a request; ‘as you have done now’ interprets एवम् एव, ‘in just this way’.

comm.t: The gods ask for two things: that every affliction of the three worlds be quelled, and that their enemies be destroyed एवम् एव, ‘in just this way’ — as Śumbha and Niśumbha have just been. They ask not for one deliverance but for a standing promise.
The request matches the Goddess’s own condition in 11.37: the boon is for the three worlds, not for the gods alone. Her answer (11.41–55) turns it into the prophecy of her future descents.

flags.uncertain: सर्वाबाधा: read as सर्व + आबाधा ‘all afflictions’ (the usual reading); सर्व + अबाधा would make no sense here.

comm.t: The Goddess grants the gods’ request. What follows (11.41–55) is her prophecy: the future forms in which she will come down to destroy the enemies of the worlds. The speech runs to the end of the chapter; chapter 12 continues it with the fruits of hearing the text.
